summary: Updates RFC 3967 so the IESG has more flexibility in accepting downward references, where a Standards Track document refers to a lower maturity document, without needing explicit mention in the Last Call. It is a BCP.

eli5.summary: A rulebook said you must announce loudly every time a top-level paper cites a lesser paper. This relaxes that rule.

questions: normative reference to lower maturity document
does a downref need to be in the last call
subtitle: Makes it optional, though still strongly recommended, to flag downward references in an IETF Last Call.

tldr.problem: RFC 3967 required downward references to be explicitly called out in the Last Call, which often forced the Last Call to be repeated with delay and no real benefit.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC makes documenting downrefs in the Last Call strongly recommended but not required, and leaves any repeat of the Last Call to the IESG's discretion.
tldr.outcome: The process in RFC 3967 is not fundamentally altered, and the IESG decides case by case whether to ask the community again.

today: RFC 8067 is a Best Current Practice and has not been obsoleted. It updates RFC 3967.

sections.title: The Downref Process
sections.content:
RFC 3967 stresses that normative references from Standards Track and BCP documents should be appropriately mature. It allows references to lower-maturity documents ("downrefs") through the IETF Last Call, where the need must be explicitly documented.

It has also become common for working groups to publish foundational documents, with terminology and architecture, at Informational status, and later Standards Track documents often need them as normative references. The explicit-mention requirement proved unnecessarily restrictive and caused repeated Last Calls.
sections.eli5: Borrowing from a not-quite-final book used to need a loud announcement, and missing it meant starting the whole vote again.

sections.title: The IESG's New Responsibility
sections.content:
Documenting downrefs in the Last Call message is now strongly recommended but not required. The responsible AD should still check for downrefs before sending the Last Call. If an undetected downref turns up during Last Call or IESG review, repeating the Last Call is at the IESG's discretion.

If the Last Call is not repeated, the status of the affected downrefs is unchanged, and RFC 3967 still applies if they are used in the future. The AD should record the omission as a comment in the datatracker.
sections.eli5: If someone forgot to announce it, the referee decides whether to redo the vote, and writes down what happened.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Referencing immature protocols can have security and stability implications. The IESG should take that into account when deciding whether re-consulting the community is useful.
sections.eli5: Leaning on an unfinished idea can be risky, so the referee should keep that in mind.

references.text: Bush, R. and T. Narten, "Clarifying when Standards Track Documents may Refer Normatively to Documents at a Lower Level", BCP 97, RFC 3967, December 2004.
